## What changed

1. Teardown review is a read-only, single-activity Temporal workflow with no automatic retries, trusted observation ports, evidence and an immutable plan digest. Refresh cancellation is an atomic conditional update restricted to `awaiting_approval`; approved proposals retain grants and history.
2. Azure C3 upload and stored-source reading use trusted tenant/environment storage bindings and Storage-audience tokens. Blob access requires exact approved account hosts in supported public, government or China suffixes, HTTPS/443, no credentials in URLs and no redirects. Missing bindings disable source storage without disabling ordinary infrastructure sessions.
3. AWS boundaries are separated into app, build, machine, scheduler, EKS cluster and EKS node families. Driver and frozen managed-policy coverage prove own-family permissions and foreign-family principal refusal. Generated policies retain escalation guards and remain below IAM's 6,144-character limit in tested partitions and maximum naming inputs.
4. GitHub source schema is additive platform migration 6, included in the normal registry and emitted SQL, with existing migrations and manual installations preserved. Operator documentation and the Platform navigation link reach the browser installation/binding form.
5. Machine documentation matches actual default ports: AWS SSM, Azure Run Command, read-only GCP OS Inventory and registered zenithd. GCP guest mutations require zenithd; Kubernetes guest execution requires an injected credential resolver.
6. OCI migration instances receive trusted runner-created bindings. Durable receipts record intent before create/delete, preserve unknown lost responses without relaunch and restrict cleanup to matching receipt-owned terminal instances. Cleanup request acceptance is not proof of deletion completion. No retention/pruning policy was introduced.
7. Verification repairs cover the dependency lockfile, bounded password redaction, browser GitHub callback routing, private short macOS Go/OpenTofu scratch paths, runner membership ordering, real Kubernetes apply/release races, migration patch semantics, composed AWS family fixtures and deterministic rollout polling. Node metadata, CI and the worker base now use a supported Node 22 patch; the Docker build includes imported SSM JSON assets.
8. Teardown page wiring tests now verify read-only persisted-review loading, browser/workspace/environment context and exact typed-name confirmation. Production code did not change in this last test repair.

## Failures encountered and resolved

- Checkpoint complete suite: 15,636 passed, 2 failed, 208 skipped in 779 files. A cold Temporal lifecycle setup also failed at suite level. The actual redaction and callback defects were fixed; affected checks and the final gate pass. An initial default-heap typecheck exhausted memory; 4 GB heap succeeds.
- The first final attempt with three Vitest workers was interrupted with exit 130 after memory/swap pressure and Docker API failures. Only completed-file partial counts exist: 6,379 passed, 23 failed, 157 skipped in 184 reported file lines. Those are not a complete-suite total. The composed AWS fixture, PGlite setup budget and timer-based rollout assertion were repaired; concurrency reduced without dropping suites or weakening functional/security deadlines.
- Completed serial attempt before the last page assertion repair: 15,851 passed, 3 failed, 194 skipped in 788 files. Two failures occurred during provider initialization and passed unchanged on root retry, including signed AWS provider bootstrap validation and 4 module tests. The third was a stale UI expectation of no initial fetch; its strengthened browser-context and confirmation assertions now pass.
- GitHub migration's first broad lane: 943 passed, 1 stale migration assertion failed, 17 skipped. Corrected assertions passed 22/22; final migration/source/docs lane passed 148 with 14 explicit gates skipped.
- The Go runtime lane initially exposed an unrelated runner ordering assertion: 335 passed, 1 failed; corrected membership contract passed 44/44. One later cold provider request hit a network deadline; the real Go provider lane passed on retry and again in the fresh pre-merge run.
- Early real kind runs exposed SSA/status races, invalid apply-only parameters on MergePatch and rollout/migration timing. Corrected owned-operation behavior passed independent contract and real-cluster checks. Loading a multiarch image index initially failed on missing foreign-platform blobs; the official pinned ARM64 manifest loaded and both suites passed.
- The first worker image build failed because 12 SSM JSON imports were absent from its build context. Adding only the required build-stage assets fixed the real Docker build. A copied-layout bundle regression reproduced the failure before the fix and passes after it.

The final complete gate and fresh kind rows above are the acceptance result. Earlier failures remain recorded rather than hidden.

## Remaining acceptance and user decisions

- Live AWS/GCP/Azure/OCI, customer builds and registry pushes, IAM/STS/KMS, state recovery, private GitHub, current real Postgres/pooler/TLS and production Temporal acceptance need approved accounts/infrastructure. Local mocks, PGlite, Temporal test services and kind do not establish those results.
- AWS boundary migration is stack-first and currently supports default unsuffixed names. Nonempty bootstrap suffixes are size-tested but not propagated into connection/compiler selection. The largest tested legacy boundary is 6,136 characters and deploy policy 5,951; recheck after changing names, partitions or hosted zones. Frozen AWS-managed attachment actions can change upstream.
- OCI requires its durable receipts on the same runner. Lost create responses remain unknown and deletion completion is unverified. No receipt or audit retention policy was chosen.
- Azure sovereign Blob hosts are validated, but sovereign authority/ARM readiness is unverified. Storage binding, data permissions and network reachability need operator configuration.
- Managed Zenith's default session opener/substrate and source-build ports remain absent. StatefulSet/managed-cluster acceptance and enforced NetworkPolicy remain open. Real machine/cloud transports are unverified.
- Legacy setup/doctor runtime checks and separate hosted SQLite/recipe admission still use older floors; root package metadata, CI and worker pinning use >=22.22.2 <23.
- User decisions are required before audit/receipt retention or pruning, live cloud use, force pushes or history rewriting. None were performed here. Saved founder landing work remains in its existing stash. No Zenith application server was started.
